title: WASCAL Calls for Strategic Partnerships at COP31 to Scale Climate and Energy Solutions in West Africa
excerpt: Accra, 4 November 2026-The West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL) will join the global climate community at the 31st Conference of the Parties
html:
Accra, 4 November 2026-The West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL) will join the global climate community at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026.

COP31 comes one year after WASCAL launched its Strategic Plan 2026–2030 at COP30 in Belém, Brazil. In Antalya, the institution will highlight its work in climate research, climate and environmental services, capacity building, renewable energy and green hydrogen, and engage with partners to scale climate action across West Africa. As an observer organisation to the UNFCCC, WASCAL contributes to the Convention’s processes and supports West African countries in advancing the goals of the Paris Agreement.

Through side events and partner sessions, WASCAL will demonstrate how it translates climate research into services for the region, including early warning systems, mobile applications, locally developed sensors, decision-support systems and climate bulletins. WASCAL will also share research findings and project experiences in energy modelling, renewable energy and green hydrogen to support West Africa’s just energy transition.

On 18 November, WASCAL’s Executive Director, Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, will deliver the organisation’s statement at the High-Level Segment of COP31. He will call for partnerships to extend climate services, research and graduate training across West Africa. During the conference, he will also hold bilateral meetings to discuss future cooperation.

“One year after launching our Strategic Plan at COP30, WASCAL comes to Antalya to show how climate research can translate into solutions that support decision-making across West Africa. Climate information only matters when it drives decisions. We invite governments, development partners, research institutions and the private sector to work with us to scale climate services, strengthen resilience and advance a just energy transition in the region,” said Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, Executive Director of WASCAL.

At COP31, WASCAL will also raise awareness of the second edition of its International Conference on Climate Change and Just Energy Transition (I3C-JET 2027) and invite the climate community to take part. The conference will take place in Cotonou, Benin, on 27–28 October 2027, bringing together researchers, policymakers, development partners, financial institutions, private-sector actors and civil society under the theme “From commitments to implementation: mobilising science, policy, finance and partnerships for climate resilience and a just energy transition in Africa”. The call for abstracts opens in November 2026.

Follow WASCAL’s COP31 activities on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram: @wascalclimate.

By Marc Belemsobgo

title: WASCAL Appoints Dr. Seyni Salack as Director of its Competence Centre
excerpt: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, 29 October 2026 -WASCAL is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Seyni Salack as Director of the WASCAL Competence Centre, effective 1 November 2026. Dr. Salack
html:
Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, 29 October 2026 -WASCAL is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Seyni Salack as Director of the WASCAL Competence Centre, effective 1 November 2026.

Dr. Salack is an accomplished climate scientist and research leader with more than 20 years of international experience in climate science, climate adaptation, resilience, early warning systems and capacity development. Since joining WASCAL in 2016, he has served as Senior Research Scientist, Regional Thematic Coordinator for Risks and Vulnerability to Climate Extremes, and Interim Director of Research and the Competence Centre.

He holds a PhD in Climate and Climatic Impacts, a Master’s degree in Atmospheric Physics and a Master of Business Administration (MBA). His expertise spans climate science and modelling, multi-hazard early warning systems, impact-based forecasting, anticipatory action, disaster risk reduction, climate–energy and climate–health systems, numerical weather and crop yield forecasting, and project management.

Dr. Salack has led major local and international initiatives. He has authored numerous peer-reviewed publications, books, book chapters and atlases that have advanced climate knowledge and resilience across Africa.

Please join us in congratulating Dr. Seyni Salack on his appointment and in wishing him every success as he advances WASCAL’s mission of scientific excellence, innovation and climate-resilient development across West Africa.

By Marc Belemsobgo

title: WASCAL and Partners Secure €2 Million to Help Farmers Build Climate Resilience in West Africa
excerpt: DAS-Clim selected among four research projects funded under the CS4RRA joint call Accra, Ghana- 28 October 2026- WASCAL and five partner institutions from West Africa and Europe have been awarded
html:
DAS-Clim selected among four research projects funded under the CS4RRA joint call

Accra, Ghana- 28 October 2026- WASCAL and five partner institutions from West Africa and Europe have been awarded a €2 million to implement the DAS-Clim (Digital Advisory Services to Strengthen Crop-Livestock Health and Climate Resilience in West Africa) project.

Co-funded by Germany, Norway and France under the CS4RRA (Climate Services for Risk Reduction in West Africa) joint call for proposals, DAS-Clim is one of only four research projects selected for funding under the call.

Over the next three years, DAS-Clim will build on digital solutions already developed and field-tested by WASCAL under the previous icipe/OACPS/EU-funded PPeDMaS (Precision Pest and Disease Management System based on Multidimensional Big Data) project in Burkina Faso. These include the PlanteSaine mobile application and the Pilot Early Warning System (PEWS), which support the early detection and management of pests and diseases affecting maize, onion and tomato.

Already used by more than 800 registered farmers and extension officers in Burkina Faso, these solutions will be upgraded and expanded under DAS-Clim. Their application will extend to Benin, while the project will introduce additional crops such as groundnuts, develop new modules for cattle health, and integrate AI-driven local-language interfaces. DAS-Clim will also expand access through basic mobile-phone services (USSD) and digikiosks, enabling communities without smartphones to benefit from timely agricultural and climate information. By combining digital technologies, climate information and security risk, and agricultural knowledge, the project will help farmers and livestock keepers better anticipate pest and disease risks, protect their livelihoods and strengthen food security and climate resilience.

Highlighting the scientific significance of the project, Dr. Seyni Salack, Director of WASCAL Competence Centre, said:

“DAS-Clim builds on innovations that have already demonstrated their value in the field and creates an opportunity to take them further. By combining climate information, digital technologies and locally accessible advisory services, the project will bring scientific knowledge closer to farmers and livestock keepers. This is an important step towards developing practical and scalable solutions that can strengthen climate resilience and food security across West Africa.”

DAS-Clim consortium brings together complementary expertise from West Africa and Europe, including WASCAL (Ghana), Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK, Germany), Norwegian Institute of Bioeconomy Research (NIBIO, Norway), French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development (CIRAD, France), International Centre for Research and Development on Livestock Farming in Sub-humid Areas (CIRDES, Burkina Faso), and the University of Parakou (UP, Benin).

The consortium is led by Dr. Kisito Gandji, Research Scientist and Head of WASCAL’s Climate Smart Agriculture and Food Systems (CSAFS) Programme.

This achievement reflects WASCAL’s continued commitment to scientific excellence, strategic partnerships and research that helps communities across West Africa better respond to climate-related risks and strengthen food security.

title: WASCAL Engages GIZ Ahead of Joint High-Level Mission to Germany
excerpt: 27th October, 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL has paid a courtesy call on Dr. Sandra Retzer, Country Director of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in Ghana, to
html:
27th October, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL has paid a courtesy call on Dr. Sandra Retzer, Country Director of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in Ghana, to discuss preparations for its upcoming joint high-level mission to Germany with the Southern African Science Service Centre for Climate Change and Adaptive Land Management (SASSCAL).

The visit is an opportunity for WASCAL to brief the GIZ Country Director on the objectives of the planned mission and seek her guidance in facilitating engagement with relevant GIZ counterparts in Berlin.

The joint mission, tentatively scheduled for 3rd or 4th December 2026, will bring together the Chairs of the Ministerial Councils of WASCAL and SASSCAL, WASCAL Patron Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, the two Executive Directors, and a supporting team.

Established through German cooperation, WASCAL and SASSCAL serve countries across West and Southern Africa, respectively, by supporting scientific research and cooperation on climate change and sustainable land management.

The engagement reflects WASCAL’s commitment to strengthening institutional partnerships and fostering dialogue with German cooperation partners in support of climate research, knowledge exchange, and sustainable development across Africa.

title: WASCAL Takes Africa’s Renewable Energy Priorities to Venice
excerpt: 22nd October 2026 By Peace Ahovi Africa’s transition to sustainable energy requires more than ambitious climate commitments. It calls for effective financing mechanisms, stronger partnerships,…
html:
22nd October 2026

By Peace Ahovi

Africa’s transition to sustainable energy requires more than ambitious climate commitments. It calls for effective financing mechanisms, stronger partnerships, innovative solutions, and practical approaches that respond to the continent’s development priorities.

At the 5th Venice Conference on Global Governance of Climate Change and Sustainability in Venice, Italy, WASCAL engaged global stakeholders on renewable energy, climate finance, and sustainable development. These issues were central to WASCAL’s participation.

Representing WASCAL at the conference, Jean Francis Sempore, Fundraising and Project Manager, joined discussions on global sustainability, with particular attention to the session “Developing Renewables in Africa: Grids, Finance and Distributed Solutions (focus on solar).”

The session, presented by students of SDA Bocconi School of Management, brought together perspectives from climate finance, impact investment, development funding and institutional stakeholders. Discussions included representatives of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), UniCredit, the Global Steering Group for Impact Investment and City Bridge Foundation London.

The engagement provided an opportunity to examine the financing and infrastructure considerations shaping Africa’s renewable energy development, particularly the role of solar energy and distributed solutions in supporting the continent’s energy transition.

Beyond renewable energy, the conference explored emerging challenges and opportunities at the intersection of climate change, technology, and sustainable development. Themes included urban adaptation and mobility, insurance, artificial intelligence and the climate transition, regenerative agrifood systems, and sustainability in a changing global climate.

For WASCAL, these discussions reinforce the importance of connecting scientific research, innovation and capacity development with the financial, institutional and technological frameworks needed to address climate-related challenges across West Africa.

The conference also offered insights into how multidisciplinary discussions, including student presentations reviewed by panels of experts from the public and private sectors, academia, media and civil society, can inform the design of scientific events, conferences and capacity-building programmes.

An important outcome of the engagement was the confirmation of interest in collaboration between the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage and WASCAL. Follow-up exchanges are expected ahead of COP31.

WASCAL also identified opportunities to strengthen coordination with Vision Think Tank to support greater institutional participation and deepen Africa-focused themes in future editions and related events. Further engagement with contacts on climate finance and other thematic areas is also planned.

The conference concluded with the presentation of the draft Venice Manifesto and the Marco Polo Award for rising global awareness, which honoured Kim Campbell, former Prime Minister of Canada, and Ibrahima Cheikh Diong, Executive Director of the FRLD.

WASCAL’s participation reflects the importance of international knowledge exchange and strategic engagement in advancing climate resilience and sustainable development in West Africa.

By strengthening partnerships, exploring climate finance opportunities, and drawing lessons from global policy and innovation discussions, WASCAL continues to connect scientific knowledge with the collaborations and practical approaches needed to address the region’s climate challenges.

title: Chair of the WASCAL Ministerial Council Is Championing Sustainable Development in Africa
excerpt: 20th October 2026 By Peace Ahovi Leadership in environmental governance and sustainable development calls for a combination of legal expertise, strategic insight, and a strong commitment to national…
html:
20th October 2026

By Peace Ahovi

Leadership in environmental governance and sustainable development calls for a combination of legal expertise, strategic insight, and a strong commitment to national and regional priorities. Hon. Djami Diallo, Chair of the WASCAL Ministerial Council and Guinea’s Minister for Higher Education and Scientific Research, brings these qualities to her work in advancing development in Africa.

Her professional journey reflects extensive experience in legal affairs, public administration, and strategic national initiatives. Before she was appointed Minister, she served as Director of Legal Affairs at the Presidency of the Republic of Guinea, advising the state on major infrastructure projects.

In June 2022, Hon. Diallo was appointed to the Strategic Committee responsible for monitoring the Simandou project, a major infrastructure and mining initiative in Guinea. Her involvement also extended to negotiations on agreements related to the project with industry partners, contributing legal and strategic perspectives to an initiative of national significance.

Her leadership experience also spans Guinea’s petroleum sector. Since April 2022, she has served as Chairwoman of the Board of Directors of the National Petroleum Company of Guinea (SONAP SA), bringing her legal knowledge and governance experience to the sector.

Hon. Diallo’s professional credentials extend beyond Africa. She was admitted to the New Jersey Bar in 2014 and the New York Bar in 2015, reflecting her engagement with the international legal profession.

In her capacity as Chair of the WASCAL Ministerial Council, her experience in environmental governance, public policy and strategic leadership provides a valuable perspective for advancing dialogue and cooperation on climate change and sustainable development across WASCAL’s member countries.

As Africa continues to address the interconnected challenges of climate change, environmental protection and sustainable economic growth, leadership that connects policy, governance and regional cooperation remains essential. Hon. Djami Diallo’s professional experience reflects the importance of these connections in shaping a sustainable future for the continent.

Strategic priorities for climate resilience, clean energy and sustainable development took centre stage as WASCAL’s Governing Board convened its 2026 Ordinary Session in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, to review institutional progress and discuss priorities for 2027.

As the organisation’s second-highest decision-making body after its Council of Ministers, the Governing Board reviewed institutional progress and discussed priorities to advance climate change solutions through Capacity Building, Research and Innovation, Climate and Environmental Services, Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen.

The session reaffirmed the importance of scientific research, innovation, and regional partnerships in strengthening climate resilience and promoting sustainable development across West Africa.

Through scientific research, capacity development, innovation, and regional partnerships, the organisation continues to advance practical climate solutions, support the transition to clean energy, and improve livelihoods across the region.

title: WASCAL Engages Regional Water Stakeholders at Freao 2026
excerpt: WASCAL participated in the first West African Regional Water Forum (FREAO 2026), held in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, from 20 to 26 September 2026, as part of a series of regional
html:
WASCAL participated in the first West African Regional Water Forum (FREAO 2026), held in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, from 20 to 26 September 2026, as part of a series of regional engagements on Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in West Africa. Represented by Jean Francis SEMPORE, WASCAL took part in the Technical Committee of Experts and Ministerial Committee meetings on IWRM, as well as the regional water forum.

The engagement provided an important platform for WASCAL to present its activities, achievements and 2026–2030 Strategic Plan to IWRM focal points from West African countries, basin agencies, and technical and financial partners. It also created opportunities to strengthen relationships and explore areas of collaboration with ECOWAS, WAEMU, CILSS, basin organisations and other regional stakeholders.

Discussions during the mission brought together WASCAL and key regional actors, including representatives of ECOWAS, WAEMU, CILSS, the African Development Bank, basin agencies, GWP-West Africa and IWMI. These engagements highlighted opportunities for stronger collaboration around water resources, climate and environmental services, data, research and innovation.

The mission also identified concrete follow-up areas, including developing collaboration frameworks with WAEMU, CILSS and the ECOWAS Water Resources Management Centre; strengthening engagement with basin agencies; and exploring continuing education opportunities for water professionals.

For WASCAL, the engagement reinforced the importance of connecting science, data, partnerships, and regional action to address West Africa’s water and climate challenges. The proposed collaboration with the ECOWAS Water Resources Management Centre will initially explore the Water-Energy-Food-Environment Nexus and data.

title: WASCAL and 2iE Forge a New Path for Climate and Sustainable Development Solutions
excerpt: 28th September 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL and the International Institute for Water and Environmental Engineering (2iE) have signed a five-year Framework Cooperation Agreement to deepen collaboration…
html:
28th September 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL and the International Institute for Water and Environmental Engineering (2iE) have signed a five-year Framework Cooperation Agreement to deepen collaboration across West Africa.

The agreement opens opportunities for joint work in training and capacity building, research and innovation, climate services and data, shared infrastructure, as well as the development of strategic partnerships and funding opportunities.

Following the signing, officials from 2iE paid a courtesy visit to WASCAL Headquarters in Accra, providing an opportunity for both institutions to exchange ideas and discuss areas where their complementary expertise can contribute to practical solutions for climate and sustainable development challenges.

During the visit, the 2iE delegation endorsed the CCAN signature poster for climate action, reaffirming a shared commitment to advancing climate awareness and collective action.

From strengthening skills and supporting research to advancing climate services, renewable energy and sustainable development, the partnership brings together complementary expertise with a shared commitment to contributing to Africa’s development.

With the framework now in place, the focus shifts from agreement to action, turning knowledge, expertise and partnerships into practical solutions for a more climate-resilient and sustainable West Africa.

Work begins now.

title: WASCAL Meets with Benin Government to Co-Organise 2027 I3CJET in Benin
excerpt: 25th September, 2026 By Peace Ahovi Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, WASCAL Executive Director, met with Hon. Dr. Romarique Sèdami Mèdégan Fagla, Minister for Higher Education and Scientific Research…
html:
25th September, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, WASCAL Executive Director, met with Hon. Dr. Romarique Sèdami Mèdégan Fagla, Minister for Higher Education and Scientific Research of the Republic of Benin, during his visit to Cotonou.

The meeting focused on strengthening WASCAL’s strategic engagement in Benin and discussions around the proposed co-organisation of the 2027 International Conference on Climate Change and Just Energy Transition (I3CJET), scheduled for 25th to 29th October 2027 in Cotonou.

The proposed conference is expected to bring together researchers, policymakers, academics, development partners, and other stakeholders to exchange knowledge and advance practical solutions to climate change and the just energy transition in West Africa.

The engagement also provided an opportunity to highlight WASCAL’s longstanding contribution to climate research, education and innovation in Benin. Over the years, WASCAL has invested nearly €5 million in the country through programmes supporting training, research and innovation.

At the University of Abomey-Calavi (UAC), WASCAL’s doctoral programme on Climate Change and Water Resources continues to contribute to specialised scientific capacity development. A WASCAL hydrometeorological station near Tanguiéta, operational since 2013, also continues to generate data supporting climate research and understanding.

Through its capacity-building programmes, 52 Beninese doctoral students and 33 master’s students have benefited from full scholarships, contributing to the development of climate and environmental expertise in the country.

The discussions explored opportunities for further collaboration in climate science, research and innovation, capacity development, climate services and the transition towards sustainable and equitable energy systems.

The proposed I3CJET 2027 in Cotonou represents an opportunity to deepen cooperation between WASCAL and Benin while creating a regional platform for dialogue on Africa’s climate and energy priorities.

WASCAL remains committed to working with its member countries and strategic partners to connect scientific knowledge with policy and practice and to advance solutions for a more climate-resilient and sustainable West Africa.

title: Côte D’ivoire Launches the Development of its National Green Hydrogen Strategy
excerpt: Côte d’Ivoire has launched the development of its National Green Hydrogen Strategy to assess the potential of green hydrogen and identify the conditions required for its development in the country.
html:
Côte d’Ivoire has launched the development of its National Green Hydrogen Strategy to assess the potential of green hydrogen and identify the conditions required for its development in the country.

The launch workshop, held in Abidjan, brought together the Ministry of Mines, Petroleum and Energy, WASCAL and the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR). The Ministry is leading the process in collaboration with WASCAL, with financial support from BMFTR.

The workshop brought together participants from public administration, WASCAL, the private sector and technical and financial partners, alongside media representatives. The strategy development process will assess Côte d’Ivoire’s potential for green hydrogen and provide a basis for defining national priorities and policy directions for the sector.

In his address, Mr Akoussi Jacob, Technical Adviser for Energy and representative of the Chief of Staff to the Minister of Mines, Petroleum and Energy highlighted the importance of developing a green hydrogen strategy based on Côte d’Ivoire’s national circumstances and priorities.

“For Côte d’Ivoire, it is neither a question of following a trend nor of mechanically transposing models developed elsewhere. It is first and foremost a matter of determining, based on our national realities and priorities, under what conditions green hydrogen could contribute to our development.”

Since 2020, WASCAL has combined research, training, technology demonstration and policy support in renewable energy and green hydrogen, including its contribution to the ECOWAS regional green hydrogen framework. The launch in Abidjan takes this work into a national policy process, with WASCAL directly supporting Côte d’Ivoire’s first national green hydrogen strategy.

Delivering the Executive Director’s message on behalf of WASCAL, Professor Koné Daouda outlined how the institution has approached renewable energy and green hydrogen through research, training, technology demonstration and policy support.

“Our approach does not stop at scientific research. It brings together training, research, technology demonstration and policy support to help create the conditions for the development of renewable energy and green hydrogen in West Africa. We are convinced that no energy transition can be sustainable without clear policy and strategic frameworks”.

The process will bring together public institutions, researchers, universities, private-sector actors, regional organisations and development partners to develop a strategy reflecting Côte d’Ivoire’s specific context and priorities.

WASCAL’s support for Côte d’Ivoire’s national strategy follows its technical contribution to the development of the ECOWAS Regional Green Hydrogen Policy and its implementation framework for 2023-2030 and 2031-2050. Côte d’Ivoire is the first WASCAL member state whose national green hydrogen strategy is being developed with direct support from the institution.

By Marc Belemsobgo

WASCAL Communication Division

title: Request for Proposal (Rfp)
excerpt: A PRIVATE OPERATOR OR A CONSORTIUM FOR THE OPERATION OF A WASTE-TO-ENERGY SITE IN GYANKOBAA, KUMASI, GHANA RFP Terms of Reference:…
html:
A PRIVATE OPERATOR OR A CONSORTIUM FOR THE OPERATION OF A WASTE-TO-ENERGY SITE IN GYANKOBAA, KUMASI, GHANA

RFP Terms of Reference: https://wascal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TERMS-OF-REFERENCE-RFP-W2E-operation-124082026_CALL.pdf

Date of Publication: 25th August 2026

Closing Date: 24th September 2026/ Extended to 10th October 2026                 

The West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL) invites qualified private companies or consortia to submit proposals for the long-term operation, management, and commercialisation of the Gyankobaa Hybrid Waste-to-Energy (W2E) Facility located in Kumasi, Ghana.

This state-of-the-art pilot facility was established under the project Hybrid Waste to Energy as a Sustainable Solution for Ghana (Waste2Energy – W2E), funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR). Developed through an international partnership led by the University of Rostock, the German Biomass Research Centre (DBFZ), SRH Berlin University of Applied Sciences, WASCAL, CSIR, UENR, ,KNUST and KsTU , the facility serves as a flagship demonstration of integrated waste valorisation and renewable energy technologies for West Africa.

About the Facility

Situated in Gyankobaa, approximately 25 km northwest of Kumasi in Ghana’s Ashanti Region, the facility integrates multiple waste treatment and renewable energy technologies to transform municipal solid waste and biomass into valuable products and clean energy. The site has been designed as both a commercial demonstration plant and a research platform supporting innovation, capacity building, and technology transfer.

The infrastructure includes:

  • Municipal solid waste reception and sorting facilities;
  • A fully operational anaerobic digestion and biogas production plant with combined heat and power (CHP) generation;
  • A hybrid solar photovoltaic power system with battery energy storage;
  • Composting and organic waste recovery facilities;
  • Plastic recycling, Refuse Derived-Fuel (RDF) and plastic pellet production systems;
  • Pyrolysis technologies for plastic and biomass valorisation;
  • Modern laboratory facilities for research, testing, and innovation;
  • Supporting logistics, water supply, administration, and utility infrastructure.

In the framework of the sustainability plan of the plant, WASCAL and its partners seek to recruit a private company or a consortium for the full operation of the plant.

Opportunity for application

Operating this facility offers to the selected operator an opportunity to access:

  • An operational hybrid Waste-to-Energy facility with significant expansion potential;
  • Multiple revenue streams from renewable energy generation, waste processing, recycling, compost production, laboratory services, and future technology commercialisation;
  • Collaboration with WASCAL and its regional network of universities and research institutions;
  • A unique opportunity to demonstrate scalable circular economy solutions for West Africa.

Eligible Applicants

title: Project name: TRANS-SAHARA
excerpt: [vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text el_class=”team-photos”] Project title: Novel WEFE Nexus-based approaches towards agroforestry management in the Greater North African Region Project duration:…
html:
Project title: Novel WEFE Nexus-based approaches towards agroforestry management in the Greater North African Region

Project duration: January 2025 – December 2027

Project status: Ongoing

Website: https://trans-sahara.eu/

Funding: Excellent Science (Horizon Europe / EU funding / Project)-Grant

Project Code/ID: 101182176 — TRANS-SAHARA — HORIZON-CL6-2024-FARM2FORK-01

TRANS-SAHARA aims to establish a groundbreaking approach for leveraging agroforestry systems to support African communities in their fight against climate change. This innovative approach is based on the well-established Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus approach, which emphasizes the primacy of ensuring water security when designing, installing and managing agroforestry systems. The translation of this conceptual agroforestry management approach into real-world applications is supported by an array of technical and non-technical innovations.

These include cutting-edge measurement methods and tools to accurately assess environmental and socio-economic impacts, scalable nature-based intervention strategies to facilitate sustainable exploitation of natural resources, and novel business models designed to secure long-term livelihoods of local communities engaged in agroforestry practices. The efficacy of the novel approach and supporting innovations will be rigorously tested and validated through a series of large-scale pilot demonstrations set to take place in key locations across Africa, including Ethiopia, Ghana, Tunisia, Chad, Djibouti and Senegal. Novel community-led engagement methods are used to support the co-design of the demonstrators and ensure deep acceptance of the innovation within local communities.

Expected outcomes will contribute to bridging the agroforestry data gaps in Africa, increased crop yield, doubling of farmers’ annual incomes, and creation of new carbon sinks across previously degraded territories. An ambitious post-project exploitation plan executed in partnership with EU and African policymakers and civil society groups foresees the immediate and widespread uptake of resulting innovations across African Union (AU) member countries and beyond by 2030. Innovation adopters will significantly enhance their communities’ resilience to threats posed by the climate emergency and stimulate highly sustainable socio-economic development across their region.

Objectives of TRANS-SAHARA

TRANS-SAHARA aims to address the challenges outlined above by using water security as an entry point to focus on agro-silvo-pastoral systems in the Greater Northern African Region (GNAR) with the overarching aim to:

      • increase the water content in regional water cycles to facilitate regeneration of degraded ecosystems;
      • develop bespoke, data-driven, scalable and economically viable agroforestry interventions in three main living labs (Tunisia, Ghana, Ethiopia) to showcase agroforestry innovations and
      • facilitate an innovation ecosystem at regional, national and global scales by embedding its approach from the outset in a participatory multistakeholder socio-economic process to support a systemic socio-technical transition.

Specific objectives

SO1: Capture, monitor and model qualitative and quantitative hydrological, geoscience, agricultural, biodiversity and socio-economic data through a novel inter- and trans-disciplinary approach to better understand the links between agroforestry management and climate change resilience, biodiversity preservation and sustainable agriculture

SO2: Develop a WEFE-Nexus based Agroforestry Intervention Design Tool for implementing scalable agroforestry management systems, taking into account local specificities within the three Living Labs across the GNAR (Tunisia, Ghana, Ethiopia), aimed at increasing water availability and ensuring a balance between agricultural productivity, socio-economic viability and sustainability

SO3 : Develop capacities for better understanding and evaluating the socio-economic and environmental performance of agroforestry by equipping local stakeholders/authorities with capabilities to collect and report agroforestry data and equipping them with entrepreneurial capabilities

Work Packages

TRANS-SAHARA is designed around nine (09) complementary work packages as shown below :

WASCAL is the lead of WP3 and is an invaluable partner to all other WPs for TRANS-SAHARA implementation. WASCAL leads activities on data identification, collection, sensing and database development. Specifically on Sensing, WASCAL is developing, in collaboration with EURAC, the Made-in-Africa sensors, adapted to low-technology conditions in Africa. Additionally, WASCAL contributes to the implementation of Living Labs and the delivery of capacity-building activities, technology transfer, and the establishment of the TRANS-SAHARA Entrepreneurship Hub to promote innovation, commercialization, and sustainable impact of Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) solutions. WASCAL is also tasked with the Validation, assessment and quality control of the heterogeneous data sets used in agroforestry systems analysis, including the validation of the Made-in-Africa sensors against the market-ready sensors.

 

Some Expected Results

      • Groundwater level monitoring sensors
      • Soil nutrient sensors with pH, N, P, K, EC, moisture and temperature parameters;
      • Offline-logging LoRaWAN gateway upgrades
      • Training materials on the operation & maintenance of the agroforestry measures
      • Training modules on development of the Made-in-Africa sensors
      • Made-in-Africa sensors business models for the Entrepreneurship Hub
      • Webinars for promoting the Made-in-Africa sensors

title: WASCAL Announces 14 Innovative Projects Selected Under Wise
excerpt: ACCRA, GHANA - 19 August 2026 - WASCAL has selected 14 youth-led projects from seven West African countries under the first edition of its Innovative Ideas Competition for Sustainable Energy
html:
ACCRA, GHANA – 19 August 2026 – WASCAL has selected 14 youth-led projects from seven West African countries under the first edition of its Innovative Ideas Competition for Sustainable Energy (WISE). The selected projects will receive grants of up to €20,000 each to support the development and implementation of innovative solutions in renewable energy and green hydrogen.

The selected projects come from Burkina Faso, Ghana, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo and will be implemented over a maximum period of 15 months..

The projects cover a diverse range of applications, including solar energy, green hydrogen and green ammonia, biohydrogen, biogas, waste-to-energy, electric mobility, clean cooking, cold-chain systems, smart agriculture, climate-resilient agriculture and youth skills development.

“The first edition of WISE demonstrates the creativity and practical problem-solving capacity of young West Africans. The selected projects show how renewable energy and green hydrogen can be applied to real challenges, from energy access and agriculture to mobility, waste management and skills development. WASCAL is pleased to support these ideas as they move towards practical implementation.”
Dr. Bruno Korgo, WASCAL Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen Coordinator

The competition was open to young West Africans, including students, academics, practitioners, scientists, technologists and entrepreneurs, as well as eligible associations and organisations across the region. Applicants were invited to propose solutions addressing priority areas such as energy access, green mobility, biomass and waste recovery, the Energy-Water-Food Nexus, productive uses of renewable energy, energy efficiency, women’s and girls’ empowerment, and innovative business models.

Proposals were evaluated based on their relevance, originality and degree of innovation, expected impact, sustainability, applicant qualifications and capacity, budget quality and realism, and overall feasibility. The assessment also considered the potential of the proposed projects to generate tangible benefits for communities, beneficiaries and the environment.

THE LIST OF SELECTED PROJECTS

WASCAL congratulates the 14 selected project leaders and recognises the efforts of all applicants who participated in the first edition of WISE. Through the competition, WASCAL seeks to create opportunities for promising ideas to move from concept towards implementation and contribute to practical, sustainable energy solutions across West Africa.

About WISE

The WASCAL Innovative Ideas Competition for Sustainable Energy (WISE) is an initiative of WASCAL’s Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen Coordination that supports innovative renewable energy and green hydrogen projects and research and development ideas across West Africa. Launched in 2025 with financial support from the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), WISE focuses on solutions that can contribute to sustainable energy development, particularly in rural and peri-urban communities.

title: WASCAL Celebrates €6.88 Million Horizon Europe Success with Rain4africa Project to Strengthen Rainfall Forecasting Across West Africa
excerpt: RAIN4AFRICA proposal recommended for EU funding with an outstanding evaluation score of 14.5/15 ACCRA, GHANA- 14 August 2026- A consortium of 13 African and international partners has been recommended…
html:
RAIN4AFRICA proposal recommended for EU funding with an outstanding evaluation score of 14.5/15

ACCRA, GHANA- 14 August 2026- A consortium of 13 African and international partners has been recommended for €6,877,980 in funding under the European Commission’s Horizon Europe programme to launch RAIN4AFRICA project, “Village-Scale Rainfall Intelligence for Climate Resilience in West Africa.”

The 48-month project will close longstanding gaps in rainfall information and forecasting at the village level, combining ground-based observations, satellite and reanalysis data, advanced modelling, and user-oriented climate services to support agriculture, water management, and disaster-risk reduction across the region.

WASCAL holds the largest individual allocation in the consortium, at €1,242,308.75, representing 18.06% of the total EU contribution. The proposal received an outstanding score of 14.5 out of 15 from independent European Commission evaluators, including the maximum marks of 5/5 for both Excellence and Impact

Beyond improving rainfall forecasting, RAIN4AFRICA will also strengthen research and high-performance computing capacity in the region, contributing to stronger climate research infrastructure and scientific capabilities across West Africa.

Commenting on the significance of the achievement for WASCAL, Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, Executive Director of WASCAL, said:

“RAIN4AFRICA is a major achievement for WASCAL and a strong recognition of the quality of our scientists and partnerships. It also reflects our sustained efforts to mobilise competitive resources to sustain research and innovation at WASCAL. As research funding becomes increasingly competitive, we must continue to diversify our funding base, build ambitious partnerships and position WASCAL to deliver solutions that respond to West Africa’s climate and development priorities,”

Dr. Seyni Salack, Interim Director of Research and Director of the WASCAL Competence Centre, highlighted the scientific significance of the result:

“Congratulations to the entire RAIN4AFRICA team for this excellent score of 14.5/15. It is a remarkable achievement and a strong recognition of the scientific quality of the proposal. But we have more work to do. Our responsibility now is to turn this success into scientific excellence, effective research and innovation delivery, and measurable impact for West Africa,”

At WASCAL, Dr. Belko Abdoul Aziz Diallo, Data Management Scientist and Head of the Programme Data Management and Digital Solutions (DMDS), served as the focal person for RAIN4AFRICA at the Competence Centre. His sustained scientific and proposal-development work was instrumental in shaping WASCAL’s contribution and helping craft a proposal strong enough to secure the highest funding share in a 13-partner consortium.

The RAIN4AFRICA outcome adds to WASCAL’s growing track record in competitive international research and innovation programmes and reinforces its role as a regional institution for climate research, innovation and scientific collaboration in West Africa. The success also reflects WASCAL’s institutional commitment to scientific excellence, competitive fundraising and high-quality delivery of research and innovation actions.

The RAIN4AFRICA consortium brings together 13 African and international organisations:

  • West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL)- Ghana
  • Ghana Meteorological Agency- Ghana
  • Réseau des Organisations Paysannes et de Producteurs de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (ROPPA)- Burkina Faso
  • Agence Nationale de la Météorologie (ANAM-BF) – Burkina Faso
  • WASCAL-DRP WACS, Federal University of Technology Akure)- Nigeria
  • AKADEMIYA2063- Rwanda
  • International Water Management Institute (IWMI)- Sri Lanka
  • Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)- Italy
  • Institut Jožef Stefan- Slovenia
  • DIGINOVE- France
  • WAZIUP EV- Germany
  • Fundación para la Investigación del Clima- Spain
  • METEOGRID SL- Spain

WASCAL looks forward to working with the RAIN4AFRICA consortium to ensure effective project implementation and to translate the project’s research and innovation objectives into meaningful impact across West Africa.

By Marc Belemsobgo

WASCAL Communication Department

title: WASCAL Supports Validation and Sustainable Land Management Innovations in Ghana
excerpt: 24th July, 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL has successfully concluded a series of final validation and exit workshops for the DecLaRe, COINS, and INTERFACES regional projects in Tamale, Ghana, reinforcing
html:
24th July, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL has successfully concluded a series of final validation and exit workshops for the DecLaRe, COINS, and INTERFACES regional projects in Tamale, Ghana, reinforcing the organisation’s commitment to advancing evidence-based climate action, knowledge exchange, and sustainable land management solutions across West Africa.

The workshops brought together the Participatory Learning Platform and other key stakeholders, including farmers, agricultural extension officers, policymakers, traditional leaders, civil society organisations, development practitioners, women and minority groups, to validate research findings. The programme also included field visits to project communities in Mion, Tolon, and Savelugu to engage beneficiaries, observe the practical application of project innovations, assess the adoption of project innovations, and discuss strategies for sustaining project outcomes beyond their completion in September/October 2026, as well as define pathways to sustain innovations beyond the projects’ implementation period.

Funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), the three regional projects have been implemented since 2023 in northern Ghana, northern Benin, and Senegal, generating scientific evidence and practical solutions to strengthen sustainable land management and climate resilience.

As part of WASCAL’s responsibility in disseminating research outcomes, Dr. David Anaafo of WASCAL played a key role in coordinating and facilitating the validation and exit processes. During the INTERFACES workshop, Dr. Anaafo presented an overview of the project’s interventions and contributions to strengthening collaboration among stakeholders within Ghana’s sustainable land management ecosystem.

The engagement included the DecLaRe dissemination workshop, the COINS validation activities, and community field visits in Mion, Tolon, and Savelugu, followed by a two-day INTERFACES validation and exit workshop hosted at the University for Development Studies (UDS), Tamale Campus.

The INTERFACES workshop focused on validating the evaluation results of the Ghana Participatory Learning Platform and discussing strategies to sustain the partnerships, learning processes, and innovations developed during the project. Discussions highlighted the Platform’s role in connecting scientific research with farmers’ experiences, local knowledge, policy perspectives, and community priorities.

Participants emphasised the need to maintain and strengthen the Participatory Learning Platform by promoting collaboration among research institutions, policymakers, extension services, farmer organisations, and traditional authorities. Recommendations included translating research findings into practical policy and extension materials, supporting farmer-to-farmer learning, documenting lessons, and scaling innovations such as fertiliser microdosing through locally grounded evidence.

The workshops demonstrated the importance of inclusive approaches that recognise farmers and local communities as active partners in generating and applying knowledge. The outcomes will contribute to an assessment report on the role of participatory learning platforms in implementation research projects.

Through these engagements, WASCAL continues to strengthen partnerships that bridge science, policy, and practice, supporting resilient livelihoods and sustainable land management across Africa.

title: WASCAL Alumni Lead Landmark Discovery of Living Coral Reefs in Benin
excerpt: 22nd July 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL congratulates its alumni, Gerard Zinzindohoue and Bôla-Nlé Christelle Akondé of Benin, on a remarkable scientific achievement that has led to the first documented
html:
22nd July 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL congratulates its alumni, Gerard Zinzindohoue and Bôla-Nlé Christelle Akondé of Benin, on a remarkable scientific achievement that has led to the first documented visual confirmation of living mesophotic coral communities on Benin’s continental shelf. This landmark discovery resolves a scientific question that remained unanswered for more than six decades and represents a significant contribution to marine biodiversity research and ocean exploration in West Africa.

Through the COREB (Coral Reefs Rediscovering and Exploration in Benin) project, Gerard, Christelle, and their research team have published the first scientific evidence confirming the existence of living mesophotic coral communities on Benin’s continental shelf, resolving a scientific question that had remained unanswered for more than 6 decades.

Historically, coral formations identified off the coast of Benin were believed to be dead. However, during a 2025 expedition employing modern underwater exploration technologies, the research team successfully documented thriving coral communities, providing the first visual confirmation of living mesophotic corals in the country’s marine ecosystem.

This landmark discovery not only reshapes scientific understanding of Benin’s coastal biodiversity but also underscores the vast potential for further marine exploration across West Africa. It highlights the importance of continued investment in ocean research, biodiversity conservation, and climate resilience in the region.

The scientific publication has already attracted international attention, with coverage by leading global media outlets, including BBC Wildlife Magazine, Inside Climate News, and The Debrief, demonstrating the discovery’s global significance.

WASCAL congratulates Gerard Zinzindohoue, Bôla-Nlé Christelle Akondé, and the entire COREB research team for this remarkable contribution to marine science. Their work is an inspiration to the next generation of African scientists and reinforces the critical role of research in uncovering and protecting the region’s natural heritage.

We encourage our partners, researchers, and the wider public to share this important achievement and help raise awareness of the importance of ocean exploration and marine ecosystem conservation in West Africa.

title: WASCAL Master’s Research Advances Sustainable Aquaculture in West Africa
excerpt: 20th July 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL proudly congratulates Ms. Débora Coelho on the successful defense of her master’s thesis, marking another significant milestone in advancing sustainable…
html:
20th July 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL proudly congratulates Ms. Débora Coelho on the successful defense of her master’s thesis, marking another significant milestone in advancing sustainable aquaculture research in Cabo Verde and across West Africa.

Her research, titled “Evaluation of the Impact of Supplementing with Navicula sp. Native to Cabo Verde on the Growth and Survival of Post-larvae of Penaeus vannamei (Boone, 1931) at the Shrimp Farm in São Vicente, Cabo Verde”, explored the potential of using locally sourced microalgae as a sustainable alternative to imported species commonly used in shrimp hatcheries.

The study demonstrated that the native strain of Navicula sp. effectively supported improved shrimp growth while maintaining high survival rates and suitable water quality. These findings highlight the promising role of indigenous microalgae in strengthening sustainable aquaculture practices, reducing dependence on imported inputs, and enhancing local production systems.

Ms. Coelho’s research contributes valuable scientific evidence that supports sustainable food systems, climate resilience, and the development of the blue economy in West Africa.

WASCAL remains committed to fostering scientific excellence through graduate education and research that delivers practical solutions to regional development challenges.

We extend our warm congratulations to Ms. Débora Coelho and wish her every success in her future academic and professional endeavors.

title: Press Release
excerpt: Accra Ghana, 1st July 2026 HON. DR. KANDEH KOLLEH YUMKELLA APPOINTED PATRON OF WASCAL Former UN Under-Secretary-General to champion West Africa’s climate action, resource mobilisation and just energy…
html:
Accra Ghana, 1st July 2026

HON. DR. KANDEH KOLLEH YUMKELLA APPOINTED PATRON OF WASCAL

Former UN Under-Secretary-General to champion West Africa’s climate action, resource mobilisation and just energy transition.

WASCAL is pleased to announce the appointment of Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella as Patron of the organisation. The honorary and non-executive appointment recognises Dr. Yumkella’s distinguished leadership and extensive international experience in sustainable energy, industrial development, climate advocacy and sustainable development.

As Patron, Dr. Yumkella will serve as a high-level advocate and strategic adviser for WASCAL. He will support the organisation in strengthening its engagement with governments, regional and continental institutions, development partners and financing institutions, while promoting strategic partnerships and resource mobilisation.

The appointment was welcomed by Her Excellency Dr. Diaka Sidibé, Minister of Higher Education, Scientific Research and Innovation of the Republic of Guinea and Chair of the WASCAL Council of Ministers, who expressed her appreciation to Dr. Yumkella for accepting to serve.

“On behalf of the WASCAL Council of Ministers, I warmly thank Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella for accepting to serve as Patron of our institution. His stature and dedication to Africa give us great confidence, and I look forward to working hand in hand with him to overcome the challenges before us and to advance WASCAL’s mission across our region.”H.E. Dr. Diaka Sidibé, Chair of the WASCAL Council of Ministers

Professor Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, Executive Director of WASCAL, described the appointment as an important milestone in the organisation’s development.

“Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella’s appointment comes at a defining moment for WASCAL and West Africa. His leadership, international standing and commitment to sustainable energy and development will help connect WASCAL’s scientific capabilities with political commitment, strategic investment and high-level partnerships. His engagement will support the organisation in scaling its impact, strengthening its long-term sustainability and contributing more decisively to the region’s climate resilience and just energy transition.” Professor Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, Executive Director, WASCAL

In his inaugural statement, Dr. Yumkella expressed his appreciation for the appointment and described the responsibility as a call to service.

“WASCAL symbolises the strength of West African scientific excellence and regional cooperation in responding to some of the most urgent challenges facing our region. Its scientific expertise, human capital and regional networks position it to inform policy, attract investment and generate tangible benefits across West Africa.” Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, Patron of WASCAL

He further noted that his engagement will focus on strengthening WASCAL’s influence in regional and continental decision-making, opening pathways to strategic partnerships and sustainable financing, and championing a just energy transition and the next generation of African scientific leadership.

The appointment supports WASCAL’s ambition to consolidate its position as a trusted regional and continental institution for climate science, climate services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, capacity building and sustainable development.

About the Patron

Dr. Yumkella brings more than 30 years of international leadership and development experience to the role. He is a former United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Chair of UN-Energy, the founding Chief Executive Officer of Sustainable Energy for All, and a former Director-General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). He also served as Minister for Trade, Industry and State Enterprises of Sierra Leone. Currently, he serves as the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Climate Change, Renewable Energy and Food Security (PI-CREF), and ECOWAS Special Envoy for the West Africa Regional Integration and Investment Summit. Throughout his career, he has been a leading global advocate for universal energy access, industrial development and climate action, working at the highest levels of government, the United Nations, business and academia.

About WASCAL

The West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL) is a West African intergovernmental organisation headquartered in Accra, Ghana. It provides comprehensive climate change solutions through capacity building, research and innovation, climate and environmental services, and the promotion of green hydrogen and renewable energy. Since its inception in 2012, WASCAL has trained over 700 West African PhD and Master’s degree holders through its graduate studies programmes and has mobilised significant resources for climate research and capacity building across the region. WASCAL operates a dedicated Competence Centre in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and works across its member states to strengthen the region’s resilience to climate change.

WASCAL welcomes Hon. Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella to this distinguished role and looks forward to working with him to strengthen the organisation’s regional impact, continental influence and long-term sustainability.

html:
18th May, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

The hybrid room came alive with inspiring stories, practical experiences, and powerful reflections as WASCAL and SASSCAL convened a joint webinar on “Advancing African Climate Expertise through Graduate Education – Insights from Graduates.”

More than just a webinar, the event became a vibrant platform where former students transformed into storytellers of impact, demonstrating how graduate education is shaping Africa’s next generation of climate leaders.

Alumni from WASCAL and SASSCAL Graduate Studies Programme took participants through their personal and professional journeys. They shared how their academic experiences equipped them with the technical expertise, confidence, and leadership skills needed to address pressing climate challenges across the continent.

One of the most remarkable moments of the webinar was witnessing the graduates communicate confidently across linguistic boundaries, expressing complex scientific ideas clearly in both English and French. Their ability to engage in multiple languages reflected the strength of WASCAL and SASSCAL’s capacity-building programmes in preparing graduates not only as researchers but as effective communicators and global climate advocates.

The alumni also showcased the real-world impact of their work after graduation. From leading renewable energy initiatives and climate adaptation projects to supporting policy development and community-based resilience programmes. Their stories demonstrated how education is translating into measurable action on the ground.

The webinar was further enriched by the presence of the Chair of the WASCAL Governing Board, Prof. Chinedum Uzoma Nwajiuba, the Executive Director of WASCAL, Prof Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, and the SASSCAL Executive Director, Prof. Nelago Indongo, whose remarks stressed the urgent need to continue investing in higher education, research, and capacity development to build a climate-resilient Africa.

Key guests echoed this call, highlighting the importance of stronger partnerships between research institutions, governments, and development partners to ensure scientific knowledge drives practical climate solutions.

As the discussions concluded, one message stood out clearly – graduate education is not only producing experts, but building changemakers, innovators, and leaders capable of driving Africa’s climate future.

Through this joint engagement, WASCAL and SASSCAL once again demonstrated that investing in people remains one of the most powerful tools for advancing climate action across Africa.

title: Training West Africa’s Future Climate Scientists at Sea
excerpt: 10th June 2026 By Peace Ahovi The WASCAL Floating University, a mobile, sea-based training and research initiative conducted aboard the research vessel “FS POLARSTERN”, is transforming climate science…
html:
10th June 2026

By Peace Ahovi

The WASCAL Floating University, a mobile, sea-based training and research initiative conducted aboard the research vessel “FS POLARSTERN”, is transforming climate science education by providing young West African scientists with hands-on research experience, reinforcing WASCAL’s commitment to building regional capacity and advancing climate expertise across West Africa.

As part of the WASCAL Master’s Programme in Climate Change and Marine Sciences, students from WASCAL’s 12 member countries embarked on an intensive two-week scientific expedition aboard Germany’s renowned research vessel, FS POLARSTERN, travelling from Mindelo, Cabo Verde, to Bremerhaven in Germany.

The expedition forms a key component of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space (BMFTR) funded Master’s programme hosted at the Atlantic Technical University (UTA) in Cabo Verde, where students combine academic learning with practical field research to better understand climate change and its impact on marine ecosystems.

During the voyage, students worked alongside leading international scientists and gained practical experience using advanced scientific equipment to investigate interactions between the atmosphere and the ocean. Activities included collecting water samples from depths of up to 4,900 metres, analysing marine biodiversity, monitoring carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations in the atmosphere and ocean, and studying ocean acidification processes linked to climate change.

Students also deployed modern technologies such as the Planktoscope, UnderwaterVisionProfiler (UVP), and stereo microscopes to identify marine organisms and better understand the changing health of ocean ecosystems.

For many students, the Floating University offered a unique opportunity to directly connect scientific theory with practical application. The knowledge gained will contribute significantly to their Master’s research on climate-related challenges affecting West Africa, including marine heatwaves, biodiversity loss, fisheries decline, and ecosystem degradation.

A major highlight of the expedition was the visit by the German Federal Minister for Research, Dorothee Bär, who engaged with WASCAL students aboard the vessel and emphasised the strategic importance of climate research, international collaboration, and practical scientific training for future climate leaders.

The expedition was led by the GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel in collaboration with leading international research institutions, including the Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research (IOW), Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel(CAU) and Senegal’s Centre de Recherche Océanographique de Dakar Thiaroye (CRODT-ISRA).

Funded by BMFTR, the WASCAL Graduate School Programme continues to build local expertise to address climate challenges across West Africa. Since its inception, WASCAL has trained over 650 climate professionals, strengthening regional climate resilience and scientific excellence.

Through initiatives such as the WASCAL Floating University, WASCAL remains committed to preparing the next generation of African climate scientists with the practical knowledge, international exposure, and research expertise needed to drive sustainable climate solutions for the region.

title: WASCAL Wins Top Innovation Award for Clean Cooking Technology at Solardays in Togo
excerpt: 9th June, 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL Bioenergy laboratory in Togo has the best equipment to combat climate change and improve livelihoods. At the just-ended international trade fair referred to
html:
9th June, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL Bioenergy laboratory in Togo has the best equipment to combat climate change and improve livelihoods. At the just-ended international trade fair referred to as “the Salon Fest’Immo and SolarDays in Togo”, organised by the Synergy of Renewable Energy Actors (SAER), WASCAL has been awarded the Prize for Best Technological Innovation in recognition of its outstanding demonstration of excellence, innovation, and professionalism.

Presented by the Organising Committee of Salon Fest’Immo and SolarDays together with members of the Special Jury, the Certificate of Distinction followed a rigorous assessment of participating exhibitors based on the quality of reception, stand arrangement, team presentation, and clarity of demonstrations.

WASCAL’s recognition was driven by its innovative contribution to clean cooking technologies through showcasing the Apeli Stove, a sustainable cooking solution designed to replace traditional open fires and inefficient stoves. Developed with the support of DBFZ Biomass Laboratories, the Apeli Stove significantly reduces harmful indoor air pollution, lowers carbon emissions, and decreases fuel consumption. The technology continues to be tested in rural communities in Togo as part of efforts to advance sustainable and climate-smart household energy solutions.

WASCAL used the opportunity to host a high-level side event, a symposium on the topic “Impacts of Climate Change, Obstacles to Sustainable Solutions and Synergies of Action for a Resilient Energy Transition in Togo.”

The symposium brought together key national institutions, private sector actors, development partners, and renewable energy stakeholders to deliberate on climate resilience, sustainable energy solutions, and pathways to strengthening collaboration for coordinated climate action. Discussions focused on identifying institutional, financial, technical, and social barriers to climate solution implementation while promoting renewable energy as a strategic lever for resilience.

Through its active engagement at “SolarDays”, WASCAL reaffirmed its commitment to transforming climate science into practical solutions that support resilient communities, sustainable energy access, and climate action across West Africa and beyond. WASCAL pledges for the Global Action on the ground.

title: WASCAL Marks World Environment Day 2026 with High-Level Climate Action Dialogue and Symbolic Tree Planting in Ghana
excerpt: 5th June 2026 by Peace Ahovi WASCAL commemorated World Environment Day 2026 in a colorful and impactful manner at its headquarters in Accra, Ghana, bringing together key stakeholders across…
html:
5th June 2026

by Peace Ahovi

WASCAL commemorated World Environment Day 2026 in a colorful and impactful manner at its headquarters in Accra, Ghana, bringing together key stakeholders across government, diplomacy, academia, development institutions, media, private sector, and youth groups to strengthen dialogue on practical climate action.

The celebration, held under the global theme “Climate Action. Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future,” featured a series of action-oriented activities, including high-level speeches, remarks from partner institutions, an intergenerational panel discussion, media engagement, a climate action pledge, and a symbolic tree planting ceremony.

The event officially opened with a welcome address by Prof. Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé, Executive Director of WASCAL, who welcomed participants and reaffirmed WASCAL’s commitment to transforming climate science into practical, scalable, and inclusive solutions through the implementation of the Climate Change Action Now (CCAN) initiative launched in 2025.

Prof. Ramdé emphasised that climate action must go beyond discussions to measurable implementation, stressing the importance of science, youth participation, diplomacy, partnerships, and community engagement in addressing growing climate challenges across Ghana and West Africa.

Participants also received remarks from Ms. Annassi Kerstin, representative of the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space (BMFTR), and the Head of Department “Energy and Hydrogen Research – Sustainable Energy Systems”, commended WASCAL for creating a platform that moves climate ambition into practical action. She highlighted Germany’s continued support for climate resilience, renewable energy, green hydrogen initiatives, climate awareness, and youth innovation across the region, especially the CCAN initiative. She declared that discussions on the proposed support were ongoing.

“We are pleased. I just got feedback yesterday that we can support CCAN itself, discussing some numbers, but we will work on that,.

Representing Ghana’s Minister for Climate Change and Sustainability, Mr. Moses Ayamba, Director of Monitoring and Evaluation, delivered remarks reaffirming the importance of collaboration and national commitment toward addressing climate challenges.

A major highlight of the event was the keynote presentation by Nana Sean Yaw Adjei Sikapa Agyeman, who delivered a thought-provoking address on bridging the gap between research and real-world implementation. He challenged stakeholders to strengthen partnerships between researchers, policymakers, communities, and the private sector to ensure climate research translates into practical solutions that improve livelihoods and build resilience.

The programme further featured remarks from partner institutions, reinforcing collective responsibility and partnership in climate action.

An engaging panel discussion on the theme “From Global Commitments to Practical Implementation – Youth, Science and Diplomacy for Climate Action” brought together experts and stakeholders to discuss practical pathways for implementing climate commitments through science, youth leadership, diplomacy, innovation, communication, and policy engagement. The session also featured remarks from the WASCAL CCAN Executive, represented by Dr. Daniel Ofori, WASCAL Senior Finance Manager, who highlighted progress and opportunities within the initiative, especially CCAN towards 2030, and WASCAL’s readiness to move beyond the sub-region to partner with funding institutions across the globe in combating climate change and improving livelihoods.

As a demonstration of collective commitment to environmental sustainability, participants joined a symbolic tree-planting exercise and a climate action pledge, reaffirming their commitment to advancing climate resilience and sustainable development.

The event concluded with closing remarks by Dr. Seyni Salack, acting Director of Research at the WASCAL Competence Centre in Ouagadougou, who encouraged continued collaboration and sustained action to build climate-resilient societies across West Africa.

Through this year’s celebration, WASCAL once again demonstrated its leadership in convening inclusive, solution-oriented dialogue that advances climate science, partnerships, youth engagement, and practical climate implementation across the region.

title: WASCAL Strengthens Marine and Climate Science Capacity Through Successful Master’s Thesis Defense
excerpt: 7th May 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL’s commitment to advancing marine and climate science capacity building in West Africa is once again demonstrated through the successful thesis defense of Ms.
html:
7th May 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL’s commitment to advancing marine and climate science capacity building in West Africa is once again demonstrated through the successful thesis defense of Ms. Nogaye Dia, a master’s student of the 4th Batch from Senegal.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Ms. Dia on this important academic milestone and her valuable scientific contribution to marine and climate research in the region.

Her research, titled “Zooplankton Community Structure, Biodiversity, and Seasonal Variability in the Senegalese Upwelling System,” investigated the composition, diversity, and seasonal dynamics of zooplankton communities within one of West Africa’s most productive marine ecosystems.

Drawing on samples collected during four scientific cruises between 2020 and 2024, the study applied advanced imaging techniques and ecological analyses to assess how key environmental factors, including temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and chlorophyll-a shape zooplankton distribution and community structure.

The findings revealed the dominant role of copepods in the ecosystem while also highlighting significant seasonal shifts in biomass and biodiversity driven by hydrographic conditions and upwelling dynamics. Importantly, the research establishes one of the first imaging-based baseline datasets for Senegalese waters, providing a critical reference for future monitoring of plankton dynamics, fisheries sustainability, and climate variability across West Africa.

Ms. Dia’s successful defense reflects strong scientific commitment, analytical excellence, and WASCAL’s continued efforts to train highly skilled researchers capable of addressing critical environmental and marine challenges in the region.

WASCAL congratulates Ms. Dia on this remarkable achievement and wishes her continued success in her academic and professional journey.

This milestone also reinforces WASCAL’s commitment to gender-balanced excellence in science, ensuring equal opportunities for both women and men in advancing climate and marine research across West Africa.

title: Towards Sustainable Mangrove and Wetland Management
excerpt: 5th May, 2026 By Peace Ahovi WASCAL continues to advance applied climate research through student-led scientific inquiry addressing critical environmental challenges in West Africa. As part of this…
html:
5th May, 2026

By Peace Ahovi

WASCAL continues to advance applied climate research through student-led scientific inquiry addressing critical environmental challenges in West Africa. As part of this effort, Ms. Akoté M’kawata Ahounga, a student from Togo and member of the fourth cohort of the Master Research Programme on Climate Change and Marine Sciences (MRP-CCMS), successfully defended her master’s thesis on “Assessing Long-Term Changes in Mangroves And Wetlands in Relation to Climate Parameters Along the Togolese Coast.”

Her research applied advanced geospatial analysis using Sentinel-2 satellite data within Google Earth Engine, combined with internationally recognized frameworks such as the IPCC vulnerability assessment and DPSIR model. Through this integrated approach, the study evaluated land use and land cover dynamics, climate risks, and the effectiveness of restoration efforts.

The findings revealed a modest increase in mangrove cover alongside a significant decline in other wetland types over time. Despite this growth, mangroves were found to be more vulnerable to climate-related risks, driven by factors such as policy and governance gaps, economic pressures, and changing climate patterns. Additional pressures, including pollution, deforestation, and hydrological changes, were shown to contribute to ecosystem degradation and reduced ecosystem services.

While ongoing restoration efforts have yielded localized environmental benefits, including improved air quality and biodiversity recovery, the study highlighted critical gaps in governance, stakeholder engagement, and planning processes. Local communities reported limited involvement and insufficient pre-restoration assessments, particularly concerning associated wetlands.

This research provides valuable insights to inform sustainable coastal management in Togo and underscores the importance of data-driven, inclusive approaches to ecosystem restoration and climate adaptation. It further reinforces WASCAL’s commitment to building scientific capacity and supporting evidence-based solutions for environmental sustainability in the region.

title: Advancing Marine Science Through Genetic Innovation in Cabo Verde

WASCAL in Cabo Verde continues to strengthen its commitment to high-quality, practice-oriented education in marine science through the delivery of an intensive module on Genetic Tools Applied to Marine Biology. The module was led by Prof. Dr. Reinhold Hanel from the Thünen Institute of Fisheries Ecology, in collaboration with Dr. Evandro Lopes of Atlantic Technical University. Their combined expertise offered students valuable insights into the application of genetic tools in understanding marine biodiversity and ecosystem dynamics.

The course featured a well-balanced mix of classroom instruction, fieldwork, and laboratory training. In the classroom, students explored key concepts such as biodiversity assessment, population genetics, and the impacts of fishing on marine ecosystems. These sessions laid a strong scientific foundation for the practical components of the training.

Field activities in São Vicente enabled students to translate theory into practice, as they conducted species monitoring exercises along coastal areas and engaged with local fish markets to better understand real-world ecosystem interactions and fisheries dynamics.

Complementing the field experience, laboratory sessions at Atlantic Technical University provided participants with hands-on training in advanced genetic analysis techniques. This practical exposure strengthened their ability to apply molecular tools in marine research, conservation, and resource management.

Prof. Hanel’s continued engagement with the WASCAL Cabo Verde programme since its inaugural cohort reflects a strong and sustained partnership aimed at advancing academic excellence and research capacity in West Africa. Together with Dr. Lopes, his contribution is instrumental in preparing a new generation of scientists capable of addressing pressing marine and climate challenges through innovation and evidence-based approaches.

This initiative underlined WASCAL’s broader mission to build scientific capacity and promote sustainable solutions for the protection and management of marine ecosystems across the region.
